data.exact_reserve_text: The profit on the technical account of GBP 38.2m (2014 restated: profit GBP 62.3m) includes a run-off surplus of GBP 16.4m for prior accident years (2014: GBP 5.2m surplus). This included a surplus of GBP 5.8m for reinsurance acceptance business and a surplus of GBP 10.6m on direct business (2014: surplus of GBP 13.4m for reinsurance acceptance business and a deficit of GBP 8.2m on direct business).
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a net prior-year run-off overall (a gross release) in 2015. The claims development triangle analysis shows a net favourable movement of approximately GBP 13.7m (gross) on accident years prior to 2014, representing around a 3.1% release on opening gross claims outstanding. The managing agent's narrative describes a run-off surplus (net) of GBP 16.4m, driven by releases on both reinsurance acceptance and direct business, although there was some adverse development in certain older years. The 2015 year also experienced two notable man-made large losses (Tianjin and Abkatun) which impacted current-year results but the prior-year run-off overall remained favourable.
raw_causal_phrases: includes a run-off surplus of GBP 16.4m for prior accident years (2014: GBP 5.2m surplus).
This included a surplus of GBP 5.8m for reinsurance acceptance business and a surplus of GBP 10.6m on direct business
There were two major losses in 2015 - the explosion in Tianjin (gross loss GBP 27m, net GBP 13m) and the explosion at the Abkatun platform (gross loss GBP 20m, net GBP 9m).
Both 2015 and 2014 suffered from a large number of significant attritional losses.
data.data_quality_notes: The authoritative movement note gives a net run-off surplus (narrative) of GBP 16.4m but does not provide a single explicit gross 'Insurance liabilities' movement figure; therefore the prior-year development figure above was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (considered a reliable fallback). The narrative surplus appears to be a net figure (after reinsurance) which explains the difference between the triangle-based gross release (~GBP 13.7m) and the narrative net surplus (GBP 16.4m). LOB-level prior-year movements are not explicitly provided by gross insurance-liability in the report except via a split between reinsurance acceptances and direct business (used above); mapping direct business to standard Lloyd's LOBs could not be made reliably from the disclosed information.
